summary: Deploy the new version with a state-only migration to keep the database schema unchanged during concurrent traffic with the old version. After retiring the old version, a SQL stage sets orphaned referrer_id values to NULL, then another SQL stage adds the ForeignKey constraint, completing the schema change to ForeignKey(User) self-reference.
write_consistency: Both old and new versions treat referrer_id as an integer column during overlap (deploy_new to retire_old), allowing unrestricted INSERT/UPDATE. After retire_old, orphaned referrer_id values are cleared to NULL, then a ForeignKey constraint is enforced, ensuring all non-NULL referrer_id values reference valid account_user primary keys.
revision_notes: Root cause: After retire_old, the add_fk_constraint stage failed because existing rows contained referrer_id values (e.g., 1000097) that did not reference any valid account_user primary key. The revised plan inserts a data cleanup SQL stage after retire_old and before add_fk_constraint, setting orphaned referrer_id values to NULL before enforcing the ForeignKey constraint.

stages.description: Retire the old version. After this, only the new version handles traffic.
Set referrer_id to NULL for rows referencing non-existent account_user primary keys to enable ForeignKey constraint.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM account_user u2 WHERE u2.id = account_user.referrer_id);

stages.description: Add ForeignKey constraint on account_user.referrer_id referencing account_user(id).
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT referrer_id_fk FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id);
